routes.label: Find the least distance to each town

question:
The one-way routes connecting towns \(A,\) \(M,\) \(C,\) \(X,\) \(Y,\) and \(Z\) are shown in the figure below (not drawn to scale). The distances in kilometers along each route are marked. Traveling along these routes, what is the shortest distance from \(A\) to \(Z\) in kilometers?

[Figure 1](figures/2024_AMC_8_Q14_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
Every arrow leads forward in the order \(A,X,M,Y,C,Z\), so we can find the least distances in that order. For any fixed final leg, taking a longer route to its starting town can only increase the total. Thus we only need the least distances already found when comparing incoming routes.

- To \(X\), the only incoming route is from \(A\), giving \(5\) kilometers.

- To \(M\), compare the direct distance \(8\) with \(5+2=7\) through \(X\). The least distance is \(7\).

- To \(Y\), compare \(5+10=15\) through \(X\) with \(7+6=13\) through \(M\). The least distance is \(13\).

- To \(C\), compare \(7+14=21\) through \(M\) with \(13+5=18\) through \(Y\). The least distance is \(18\).

The final arrow into \(Z\) must come from \(M\), \(Y\), or \(C\). The least totals for these three possibilities are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{through }M &: 7+25=32,\\
\text{through }Y &: 13+17=30,\\
\text{through }C &: 18+10=28.
\end{aligned}
\]
These comparisons include every incoming arrow at each town, so no allowed route is missed. The smallest total is attained by \(A\to X\to M\to Y\to C\to Z\), whose length is
\[
5+2+6+5+10=\boxed{28}\text{ kilometers}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{A}\).
